speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing right groin pain and had an abnormal leg positioning after a rear-end collision; can you describe exactly how your leg was positioned when the pain started?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Femoral Neck Fracture.

The mechanism of injury (restrained driver in a rear-end collision) combined with immediate severe groin pain and abnormal leg positioning is highly specific for a hip fracture, likely a femoral neck fracture which can sometimes present with less obvious external deformity than other fractures. I am ready to proceed with imaging confirmation if you wish, or I can finalize the diagnosis based on this high probability.
